newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK democrats challenge laws of handover legislaturE.
newsitem.headline: HK democrats challenge laws of handover legislaturE.

text.p: Hong Kong's Supreme Court ruled on Thursday that the popular Democratic Party could use government funds to challenge laws passed by a China-appointed shadow legislature for the territory.

The party won financial aid to challenge the legality of bills passed by the shadow chamber while the territory was still under under British rule, Albert Ho, a party member in the current Legislative Council, told Reuters.
Britain returns Hong Kong to China on July 1, ending 156 years of colonial rule.

China set up the shadow body, or provisional legislature, last December to replace the fully-elected Legislative Council, elected in 1995 after Governor Chris Patten introduced democratic reforms in defiance of Beijing.
The provisional assembly has started handling bills for post-handover Hong Kong, including controversial curbs on civil liberties introduced by future leader Tung Chee-hwa.
Tung was picked by a Beijing-supervised caucus to govern the territory after July 1.
Democrats say it is constitutionally illegal to have two legislatures passing laws at the same time and want bills passed by the provisional body before July 1 to be declared null and void.

"One of the objectives is to show that is obviously wrong for the provisional legislature to seek to embark on legislative activities before the first of July because it has no legal footing at all," Ho said.
The shadow legislature has been meeting regularly across the border in the southern China city of Shenzhen to avoid legal challenges.
